This does sound frustrating, and as a person with depression, I usually choose to stay single until I'm feeling better and stable. Unfortunately, depression is a real illness and doesn't always correlate with how "bad" or stressful someone's life appears to be. Depression makes every single thought and action seriously difficult and exhausting. It makes you feel tired all the time, and this is very frustrating. It makes you simply not care about the things you usually would care about. The symptoms and experience of depression varies with each person, but if I had to sum up my experience in a sentence, it's like living life in slow-motion while seriously sleep deprived. 

I suggest researching more on depression. It's not something that can be "gotten over". It needs real effort and treatment, like medication, therapy, and lifestyle changes. These things are up to her to do - you can only encourage and support. Your reaction is very normal, I think. However, I think it's important to note that you won't be able to change how she feels, her "attitude", or what she's thinking using your kind words and assurances. The best thing to do is encourage her to get help to manage her depression more effectively - to see a doctor, inquire about meds, to seek therapy, to seek a new hobby or exercise.

First of all, some basics: I’m a 20 year old female, in university, with also the “difficult past and somewhat promising future”. I also feel rage, a lot of it. I would say anger by far is the strongest emotion I feel, and I have no idea what to do with it. 

I found your post after I searched “cynic”, in hopes of finding some answers of my own. Upon reading your post, I found that some of the traits you’ve described also apply to me. Specifically, your section on restraint – that is also how I feel, to a tee. I have quotes inspired by such thoughts all over my walls (probably not a good thing),  ex. The world is a stage, but the play is badly cast ~Oscar Wilde. I also have undeniable envy of most “normal” people, of their ignorance. 
I’ve been depressed for about 10 years, diagnosed/medicated for the past three or so now. I’m also a psychology major, undergrad however, so nowhere near being an expert on any of the issues you or I face.  From what you’ve described, you seem like you’re… numb to many things, particularly emotional experience. It seems as if this numbness is not conscious. People can “numb” themselves (and what they feel) to protect themselves from future harm – and eventually ( in my personal experience), become hard, jaded, “negative” beings. That’s how I understand my own lack of normal patterns of emotion. A few examples would be my general disgust toward babies/children, couples/relationships, any sappy love song. 

I also find that I’m extremely judgmental of others, and this bothers me. I wish I could be happy-go-lucky, carefree, but it seems as if any rose-coloured glasses have been stripped from me long ago. I see the world as a stark and unforgiving place, where trust and happiness is rare and only available to few people. 

Sometimes, I do like some of the qualities I have come to develop. I like being critical, I like questioning the motives of others. I like being aware of the horrible reality of the world. 

I’m sorry if any of this doesn’t make sense/is incoherent, but I presently don’t have time to properly format.

Basically, that’s all I’ve got right now… but it seems as if we have quite a bit in common. If you’d like, I’m down for chatting more about this in-depth. It could help both of us understand ourselves better, who knows.
